lesson.menu_title: Eating Out Abroad -- A Business Dinner in Lyon
lesson.menu_desc: Dinner with a client at a bistro in Lyon: read a French menu, ask about the dishes, and make smart guesses with must, might, and can't ('It must be a local delicacy' / 'That can't be the main course') -- 35 slides
lesson.subtitle: Lesson 23 -- Eating Out Abroad
lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Lucimara | Lesson 23 -- Eating Out Abroad

listenings.text: Good evening, and welcome to Le Petit Bouchon. Tonight, our tasting menu has five courses. The first course is a green salad with warm goat cheese. The second course is a local delicacy, the quenelle. It is a light fish dumpling in a creamy sauce. It is quite rich, so the portion is small. For the main course, we have chicken cooked in red wine. After that, we serve cheese from the region, and for dessert, a praline tart. It is pink, and it is very sweet. Each course comes with a wine pairing, chosen by our sommelier. The tasting menu is sixty-five euros per person, and the wine pairing is thirty euros more. Please tell me if you have any allergies or dietary restrictions.

When a client invites you to dinner in Lyon, remember three things. First, a business dinner in France is not fast. It can take three hours, so do not plan anything after it. Second, try the local food. If you see a dish you do not know, ask the server. It might be your new favorite food. And if a dish is too rich for you, just eat a small portion. Nobody will mind. Here is a simple rule: if a small bistro is full on a Tuesday night, the food must be very good. Third, the money. In France, the person who invites usually picks up the check. So if your client invited you, say thank you, and do not offer to split it. Next time, you invite your client, and you pick up the check.

extra_audio.text: First, I arrive at the bistro and say the name on the reservation. Then, the server brings the menu, and I ask about the local delicacy. Next, I choose the tasting menu with a small wine pairing. After that, we talk about business between the courses. Finally, my client picks up the check, and I say thank you.
